html:
Nutcracker Man, known to scientists as OH 5, is the skull of an early human relative found by Mary Leakey in 1959 at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania. Its dating showed that the human family tree was far older than most people had thought.

Mary and Louis Leakey had searched Olduvai for decades. The skull had huge cheek bones, a crest on top for big jaw muscles and giant flat back teeth, hence the nickname. Louis named it Zinjanthropus boisei; it is now placed in the species Paranthropus boisei, a side branch of the family. Later tests of its teeth suggest it ate mostly tough grasses and sedges rather than nuts.

In 1961 the volcanic layers around it were dated by the new potassium-argon method to about 1.75 million years old, roughly twice what many experts expected. The find brought fame and funding to the Leakeys and turned East Africa into the centre of the search for human origins, leading to Homo habilis at the same site and later to Lucy in Ethiopia.
